entries.title: Psalms 70:1
segments:
, to the notes on which the reader is referred. 
 
Verse 1. Make haste to help me] I am in extreme distress, and the most imminent danger. Haste to help me, or I am lost.

entries.title: Psalms 70:2
segments: Verse 2. Let them be turned backward] They are coming in a body against me. Lord, stop their progress!

entries.title: Psalms 70:3
segments: Verse 3. That say, Aha, aha.] hah hah heach! heach! a note of supreme contempt. See on

entries.title: Psalms 70:4
segments: Verse 4. Let God be magnified.] Let his glory, mercy, and kindness, continually appear in the increase of his own work in the souls of his followers!

entries.title: Psalms 70:5
segments:
Verse 5. But I am poor and needy] Nwybaw yne ani veebyon, I am a poor man, and a beggar-an afflicted beggar; a sense of my poverty causes me to beg. 
 
  Thou art my help] I know thou hast enough, and to spare; and therefore I come to thee. 
 
  Make no tarrying.] My wants are many, my danger great, my time short. O God, delay not! 
 
ANALYSIS OF THE SEVENTIETH PSALM 
 
The contents of this Psalm are the following:- 
 
I. The prayer of David for himself, that he may be freed from his enemies,

. 
 
II. For the speedy overthrow of the wicked

. 
 
III. For the prosperity of the godly,

. 
 
IV. The arguments he uses to induce God to answer his prayer. 
 
1. His miserable condition: "I am poor and needy." 
 
2. God's office: "Thou art my Helper and Redeemer."
